input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. On completion,
each flow is fully operable with keyboard alone — focus is managed correctly in
modals, no control is unreachable, and focus indicators render consistently —
bringing the flows into the fixed state that the updated conformance
documentation will describe.

## Scope

- Fix all focus-trap and focus-loss defects in the modals and dialogs of the
  four audited flows, per the audit report's per-flow defect enumeration.
- Make every control in the four audited flows reachable and operable via
  keyboard (tab order, key handlers, escape/cancel paths).
- Apply a consistent visible focus-indicator treatment across the controls of
  the audited flows, eliminating the inconsistencies the audit found.
- Verify no keyboard-interaction regressions in the surrounding Dashboard
  surfaces touched by these changes.
- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and flows
  outside the four audited ones, are out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using
  keyboard only, with no focus traps and no unreachable controls, as verified
  against the audit report's defect list (every enumerated defect is resolved
  or explicitly dispositioned).
- Focus indicators are visibly consistent across all controls in the four
  audited flows (same indicator treatment for the same control roles).
- A recorded manual keyboard-only walkthrough of each of the four flows passes.
- Existing Dashboard test suites pass with the changes in place (no
  regressions).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P1): the four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls — this epic's core scope.
- **HLR-2** (P1): visible focus indicators consistent across the audited
  flows — covered by the focus-indicator scope above (bundled with HLR-1:
  same surface, same controls, same change).

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation —
the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) and the product docs
accessibility statement — to reflect the fixed state of the four core Dashboard
flows after the keyboard accessibility remediation is complete. The published
conformance statement is a renewal requirement for two public-sector customers,
so the republished documentation is a first-class deliverable of the strategy,
not an incidental touch-up.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT entries for the four remediated flows (project creation,
  workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) to reflect the
  post-fix keyboard operability and focus-indicator conformance state.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the
  current supported state and any remaining known limitations outside the four
  audited flows.
- Republish both artifacts through the Red Hat docs content process.
- Content outline (inside Scope, per artifact contract):
  - VPAT: conformance claims per applicable success criteria for the audited
    flows, marked against the remediated state.
  - Accessibility statement: summary of keyboard support for the audited
    flows, out-of-scope limitations, and contact/reporting path.
- Technical review of the documented claims against the implemented fixes
  before publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to reflect the fixed state of the four audited flows and
  republished at its public location.
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated and republished.
- The documented conformance claims are technically reviewed against the
  implemented keyboard accessibility remediation, and the review sign-off is
  recorded (reviewer and date).
- The published documents contain no claims that contradict the implemented
  state of the four flows.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3** (P2): the accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed
  state, with technical review — this epic's full scope.
